title: Homogeneous attractive Bose-Einstein condensates with repulsive three-body interactions: the one-dimensional case
abstract: We investigate the behavior of a homogeneous one-dimensional Bose gas composed of $N$ identical bosons experiencing attractive two-body and repulsive three-body interactions. Utilizing intermediate Hartree theory, we rigorously derive the homogeneous cubic-quintic nonlinear Schrödinger functional as the mean-field limit of the many-body Hamiltonian. Particular attention is given to the impact of the repulsive three-body term on ground state energy estimates and mass concentration properties
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the ground state of a 1D Bose gas with competing attractive two-body and repulsive three-body interactions. By employing advanced techniques like intermediate Hartree theory and Onsager inequalities, the authors rigorously prove that the quantum energy converges to a mean-field limit described by a cubic-quintic nonlinear Schrödinger equation. This establishes a powerful mathematical framework for understanding complex many-body quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the ground-state properties of a one-dimensional homogeneous Bose gas subjected to competing attractive two-body and repulsive three-body interactions.
main_result: The quantum ground state energy per particle is shown to converge to the mean-field limit described by the cubic-quintic nonlinear Schrödinger functional in the large-N limit.
method: The analysis employs intermediate Hartree theory and utilizes Onsager-type inequalities to bridge the gap between the full many-body Hamiltonian and the mean-field functional.
model_or_system: The system is a homogeneous Bose gas of N identical bosons in 1D, governed by a Hamiltonian containing both two-body (attractive) and three-body (repulsive) interaction terms.
key_observables: Ground state energy per particle ($E_{QM}$), density profile ($ho_N$), and the resulting mean-field energy functionals ($E_{NLS}$, $E_{TF}$).
important_parameters: Interaction strengths ($a$ for two-body, $b$ for three-body), particle number ($N$), and scaling parameters defining the limiting regimes (e.g., $b_N 	o b_0$ or $b_N 	o +\infty$).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the intermediate Hartree approximation and the use of Onsager-type inequalities, which are necessary because the system is unconfined and translationally invariant.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first deriving the mean-field limit (cubic-quintic NLS functional) from the many-body Hamiltonian using Hartree theory. It then rigorously proves the convergence of the quantum ground state energy to this mean-field limit, analyzing both the general cubic-quintic regime and the Thomas-Fermi limit separately.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools to analyze the stability and ground state structure of interacting quantum gases, particularly when higher-order (three-body) interactions are present, which is crucial for understanding real-world BEC experiments.
